name: OpenCV
summary: A C++ computer-vision library centered on dense n-dimensional Mat data, generic InputArray/OutputArray interfaces, modular algorithms, parallel execution, and backend-mediated video I/O.
scope: Mat dense array and memory model

features.name: Strided dense Mat array model
features.description: cv::Mat represents n-dimensional dense single- or multi-channel arrays with dimensions, element type, step metadata, reference-counted storage, submatrix headers, and explicit clone for deep copies.
benefits: Provides one data model for images, matrices, volumes, and other dense numerical arrays
Supports views and in-place processing without requiring every operation to copy data
costs: Shared headers and submatrices require careful lifetime and continuity reasoning
Type, channel, stride, and ownership choices affect algorithm compatibility

features.name: Generic InputArray and OutputArray boundary
features.description: OpenCV algorithm APIs accept InputArray and OutputArray wrappers that can be constructed from Mat, vectors, GPU matrices, and other supported array forms; output creation is delegated through the output abstraction.
benefits: Allows algorithms to accept multiple storage representations through one API shape
Separates public algorithm signatures from concrete allocation details
costs: Conversion and backend support can vary by input kind
Generic wrappers hide ownership and allocation behavior that callers still need to understand

features.name: Modular algorithms with parallel dispatch
features.description: The source separates core, image-processing, and other modules; core exposes parallel_for_ and Mat::forEach hooks, while algorithm implementations can use the common dispatch layer.
benefits: Provides reusable algorithm modules over common array contracts
Offers parallel execution without forcing every caller to manage worker scheduling
costs: Performance depends on build options, data layout, and backend availability
Module boundaries and dispatch layers add configuration and debugging complexity

features.name: Backend-mediated video capture and writing
features.description: VideoCapture and VideoWriter expose open, read/write, property, and release operations while selecting API backends such as FFmpeg, GStreamer, camera APIs, or image sequences. The implementation includes plugin ABI/API checks and backend loading.
benefits: Provides a stable stream API across files, devices, and network sources
Allows platform-specific codecs and devices behind backend adapters
costs: Effective behavior and properties vary by backend, driver, codec, and device
Plugin compatibility and availability affect runtime portability

mathematical_views.question: How do shape, type, channels, and step metadata determine addresses and views over dense data?
assumptions: A Mat header describes a dense region with a step per dimension
Submatrix operations may share storage with a parent
The view abstracts allocator and SIMD implementation details

mathematical_views.question: Which concrete array representations can participate in a common algorithm call?
assumptions: InputArray and OutputArray define accepted conversion and allocation operations
Algorithms reason through the wrapper rather than a single storage class
The model does not claim all algorithms support all wrapper kinds equally

mathematical_views.question: How does an algorithm's range of work map to an available parallel backend?
assumptions: A range can be partitioned into stripes or worker tasks
The dispatcher chooses among compiled backends or a serial path
The view abstracts scheduling fairness and hardware-specific kernels

mathematical_views.question: How does a video stream transition from backend selection to opened, read, property, and released states?
assumptions: A VideoCapture or VideoWriter instance delegates to one selected backend
Backend properties may be unsupported or interpreted differently
The model abstracts codec and device protocol internals

benefits: Flexible dense numerical representation with views
costs: Aliasing, strides, and type metadata complicate correctness
Generic wrappers can obscure concrete allocation and support constraints

benefits: Reusable modules and optional parallel speedups
costs: Build and runtime configuration influence performance and behavior

benefits: Portable stream API over heterogeneous sources
costs: Backend and device variation weakens uniform guarantees
